items.title: Live: Spain receives World Cup trophy from Trump after final win over Argentina
items.description: Spain wins the 2026 World Cup, with Ferran Torres coming off the bench to score the winner in extra-time against 10-man Argentina. Follow live.

items.title: Fears massive US private lending market sinking
items.description: The corporate regulator is concerned about the risks posed by private credit for Australians with superannuation.

items.title: Abbott amplifies Hanson problem for Liberals
items.description: Pauline Hanson's grievance politics is a challenge for Labor, but a splitting headache for the Liberals — compounded by former prime minister Tony Abbott.

items.title: I tried to get unapproved injectables from a doctor. It was too easy
items.description: The booming industry selling Australians on treatments to live longer is exploiting significant gaps in health regulation, exposing consumers to risk.

items.title: Live: Joyce says One Nation does not support White Australia policy
items.description: Barnaby Joyce says his party does not support the White Australia policy after Pauline Hanson blamed the end of the policy for Australia's migration issues. Follow live.

items.title: Pauline Hanson 'not backing away' from controversial far-right interview
items.description: The One Nation leader was a guest on the podcast of controversial far-right UK figure Tommy Robinson, where she lamented the end of the White Australia policy.

items.title: For some in Australia, hope is fading and anger is rising
items.description: Sulaiman Zandinan says Australia is amazing. Wendy Newman says people in the bush are "not country bumpkins". The ABC is inviting you to have Your Say about the issues, challenges and opportunities that shape your life in 2026.

items.title: US ally Jordan summons Iranian ambassador after missile strikes
items.description: The US warns its citizens to stay away from air and sea ports at Aqaba in southern Jordan, hours before Israeli authorities announced that Iranian missiles had been launched towards the city.

items.title: Australia is making humanoid robots in the midst of its AI reckoning
items.description: Australia this week made an important step forward in grappling with the AI revolution. Meanwhile, in Melbourne a company is making humanoid robots.

items.title: Lesbian couple told they are no longer the same family by fertility clinic
items.description: The Queensland Health advice, given to fertility providers to help navigate the state's assisted reproductive technology legislation, has had a "devastating" impact on some same-sex couples trying to have more children.

items.title: Alone, robbed, and in pain: A man finds himself on Sydney's streets
items.description: People with lived experience of homelessness say the issue is deepening, as housing stock remains out-of-reach and community providers are left struggling to cope with demand.

items.title: Home Affairs asks DV survivors to prove abuser relationship 'genuine'
items.description: A federal government safety net has been identified as one of the biggest stressors for migrant women experiencing domestic and family violence.

items.title: Why the Tate brothers were arrested and what they are charged with
items.description: Everything you need to know about the arrest of the Tate brothers for alleged rape and trafficking.

items.title: Holocaust museum staff and volunteers targeted by hateful comments
items.description: Melbourne Holocaust Museum has had to step up security since 2020 following a rise in incidents that have seen threatening voice messages and hateful comments left online.

items.title: Paris fashion, Indian slums and far-right movements: Race Around the World's films
items.description: From Mexican wrestling to Indian slums, catch up on every week seven film from Race Around the World.

items.title: How to switch off and improve work-life balance when your job is online
items.description: When being across trends in your industry feels like part of your job, it can feel like work never ends. Here's how to protect your free time.

items.title: Try this week's history quiz (we made it an easy one)
items.description: Consider yourself a history buff? Test your smarts on the first Moon landing, John Howard and the Riot Act.

items.title: Asylum seekers sent Australia to Nauru say they are going hungry
items.description: According to a survey of 78 asylum seekers on Nauru, 99 per cent are regularly skipping meals because they cannot not afford to buy enough food, while more than three-quarters rarely have access to free, clean drinking water.

items.title: Live: War and AI worries drag down Wall Street, ASX set to rise
items.description: Wall Street retreated on Friday as investors continued to bail out on the AI sector. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Ken Hinkley to be announced as inaugural Tasmania Devils coach
items.description: The former Port Adelaide coach will be formally unveiled as the inaugural coach of the Tasmania Devils this morning. It completes a year long hunt for a senior coach for the AFL's newest club.

items.title: Russia pounds Kyiv in major ballistic missile attack
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia battered Ukraine's capital Kyiv overnight into Sunday local time, with one of its biggest ballistic missile barrages of the war.

items.title: Fox takes out British Open, denies Aussie after 'two perfect shots'
items.description: Ryan Fox shows nerves of steel to claim the British Open as Australia's Lucas Herbert has a near miss.

items.title: Vingegaard forced out of Tour after fracture in 'devastating' crash
items.description: Jonas Vingegaard's Tour de France campaign comes to an end after a crash on the 15th stage.

items.title: Road plan for new airport 'flawed and shortsighted', critics say
items.description: Some transport planners say the design of a major Western Sydney road upgrade is "nonsensical" and is at odds with the government's commitment to public transport and new housing.

items.title: Teacher aides face rise in kicking, biting from students
items.description: About four hundred staff — the majority teacher aides — have complained to the United Workers Union since April about facing violent behaviour from students and parents.
